report: Lateralisiert stehende Patella. Ansonsten regelrechte Artikulationsverhältnisse. Tiefgreifender, bis an den knochenreichender Knorpeldefekt an der lateralen Patellafacette großflächig mit bis zu 1,7 cm und chondralen Fibrillationen (4/8). Angrenzend teils geringes Knochenmarködem (5/8). Femorotibial regelrechte Stellung. V. a. horizontale Rissbildung des Innenmeniskus in der Pars intermedia am Übergang zum Hinterhorn (5/26, 8/9 oder 3/125). Keine dislozierten Anteile. Kein Korbhenkelriss. Keine relevante Chondropathie femorotibial. Geringes subkortikales Ödem im medialen Tibiaplateau. Kreuzbänder intakt. Außenmeniskus intakt. Kollateralbänder intakt. Geringe Flüssigkeit um das MCL, DD bei Reizzustand. Signalanhebungen am Ansatz der Quadrizepssehne und am Ursprung der Patellasehne (8/28), in erster Linie bei Reizzustand. Flüssigkeitseinlagerungen in die umgebende Subcutis. Deutlicher Gelenkerguss mit im medialen und lateralen Recessus gelegenen kleinen länglichen Strukturen (3/25). Umgebende Muskulatur und Subkutis unauffällig.

Central supporting system  
  Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): chronic complete tear with ligamentous resorption. 
  Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): unremarkable.  
  Anterior tibial translation: about intact8cm 
  
 Medial compartment  
  Normal marrow SI of medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau are preserved.  
  Medial meniscus: horizontal tear at the body and posterior horn. 
  Medial collateral ligament: preserved.  
  Medial gastrocnemius: preserved.  
  Semimenbranosus tendon: preserved.  
  Semitendinosus tendon: preserved.  
  
 Lateral compartment  
  Normal marrow SI of lateral femoral condyle and lateral tibial plateau are preserved.  
  Preservation of cartilage at weightbaring lateral femoral condyle and lateral tibial plateau.  
  Lateral meniscus: preserved.  
  Lateral collateral ligament: preserved.  
  Popliteus tendon: preserved.  
  Poplitiofibular ligament: preserved.  
  Posterior meniscofemoral ligament: unremarkable  
  Biceps femoris: unremarkable.  
  Iliotibial band: Intact.  
  Lateral gastrocnemius: intact.  
  Tibiofibular joint: unremarkable.  
  
 Patellofemoral compartment 
  Minimal effusion within patellofemoral joint extending to suprapatella bursa.  
  Quadriceps tendon: intact. 
  Patella tendon: intact. 
  Medial and lateral patellofemoral retinaculum: preserved.  
  
 Others  
  No segond fracture is identified. 
  Muscles appear unremarkable.  
  Neurovascular bundles are intact.  Chronic complete tear of the right ACL with ligamentous resorption. 
  About intact8cm anterior tibial translation 
  Horizontal tear at the body and posterior horn of the right medial meniscus. 
  Minimal right knee joint effusion.

FINDINGS:

There is a large knee joint effusion with synovitis. There is a nonruptured popliteal cyst.

There are severe degenerative changes in the medial and patellofemoral compartments with full-thickness cartilage loss and subchondral reactive changes. There is lateral subluxation and lateral tilt of the patella. There is moderate cartilage thinning involving the lateral compartment with a large cartilage defect of the central aspect of the lateral tibial plateau.

There is diffuse intrasubstance degeneration, maceration and degenerative tearing of the medial meniscus with meniscal extrusion. The lateral meniscus demonstrates intrasubstance degeneration of the body without a well-defined linear tear.

There is intrasubstance mucoid degeneration of the ACL. There is no evidence of acute ligament injury.

Otherwise the PCL, the extensor mechanism, the medial collateral ligament, the pes anserine tendons, the semimembranosus, the popliteus, the distal biceps femoris, the lateral collateral ligament and the IT band are unremarkable.

CONCLUSION:

1. Severe degenerative changes in the medial and patellofemoral compartments with full-thickness cartilage loss.

2. Diffuse degenerative tearing with maceration and extrusion of the medial meniscus.

3. Intrasubstance mucoid degeneration of the ACL without evidence of acute ligament injury.

4. Knee joint effusion with synovitis with a nonruptured popliteal cyst.

In the medial compartment, there is bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus, at the anterior horn, body and posterior horn of the meniscus is not torn and there is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. 
 The lateral compartment, there is radial tear at the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. There is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. 
 The patellofemoral joint, the patellar and trochlear cartilage appears congruent without chondral lesion. The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact.  
 In the intercondylar notch, there is complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament, at mid substance. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact.  
 The medial and lateral collateral ligament complexes are intact. The extensor mechanism is normal.  
 No knee effusion is present. The surrounding musculature is normal. There is no fracture or bone contusion.   -- Bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus, left knee. 
 -- Radial tear at the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus.  
 -- Complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament, at mid substance.

FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Moderate joint effusion with mild synovial thickening. Tiny amount of fluid in the pes anserine bursa. No popliteal cyst.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
There is a peripheral vertical tear involving the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. It is located 3 mm from meniscocapsular junction.

Bone contusions in the posterior aspect of the bilateral tibial plateau.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
As above.

None

CONCLUSION:

Interprétation : 

Il n'y a pas d’épanchement intra-articulaire ni kyste de Baker significatif. 

Les ménisques interne et externe sont intacts et sans déchirure.

Le ligament collatéral interne, le complexe ligamentaire collatéral externe de même que les ligaments croisés antérieur et postérieur sont intacts et sans déchirure.

L’alignement patellofémoral parait dans les limites de la normale.

Les surfaces cartilagineuses sont préservées, sans atteinte transfixiante ni changement sous-chondral réactionnel associé.

Les tendons du quadriceps distal et patellaire sont intacts et sans déchirure.

Conclusion :

La résonance magnétique du genou gauche est dans les limites de la normale, sans dérangement interne. 

Il n'y a pas d’épanchement intra-articulaire.

Trouvailles: 
Il y a une apparence hétérogène de la moelle osseuse plus proéminent impliquant le fémur distalement. Il n'y a pas de composante tissulaire extra-osseuse. Il y a changements similaires mais moins marqués impliquant le tibia et le péroné proximalement. 
Il y a un petit épanchement intra-articulaire sans kyste poplité. Il y a un kyste ganglionnaire multi-loculé de 2cm AP x 1.8cm transverse x 1cm cranio-caudal au niveau de la région intercondylienne antérieure. Aucune évidence de déchirure méniscale associée. Le kyste semble être en provenance des fibres distales du ligament croisé antérieur. 
Il y a proéminence et fragmentation de la tubérosité tibiale sans oedème osseux compatible avec une ancienne maladie de Osgood-Schlatter. 
Autrement, le ligament croisé antérieur, le ligament croisé postérieur, le mécanisme des extenseurs, le ligament collatéral interne, le semi-membraneux, le muscle et tendon du poplité, le biceps fémoris distal, le ligament collatéral externe et la bandelette ilio-tibiale sont sans particularité. 
Conclusion: 
1. Il n'y a aucune déchirure méniscale ou blessure du croisé antérieur. 
2. Kyste ganglionnaire au niveau de la région inter-condylienne antérieure qui semble être en provenance du croisé antérieur. Ceci pourrait causer des douleurs surtout en extension complète du genou. À corréler cliniquement. 
3. Séquelles d'ancienne maladie d'Osgood-Schlatter. 
4. Découverte fortuite d'une apparence hétérogène de la moelle osseuse. Ceci est non-spécifique et pourrait représenter une reconversion en moelle rouge. Un processus infiltratif est moins probable mais demeure dans le diagnostic différentiel. Une investigation hématologique est recommandée.

An incomplete discoid but otherwise unremarkable looking lateral meniscus is appreciated. No medial meniscal tear.

Intact cruciate and collateral ligaments, popliteus musculotendinous unit, distal iliotibial band and the extensor tendons.

No skeletal abnormality of note.
Reasonably well-maintained tricompartmental hyaline articular cartilage surfaces, especially when considering the patient's age.

A thin lobulated fluid signal intensity lesion is present in very close proximity to the pes anserine tendons, extending deep to the distal posterior oblique and superficial medial collateral ligaments, most likely representative of a bursa. 

Suprapatellar fat pad impingement is also suspected, any history of anterior knee pain?

A mild proximal insertional strain at the femoral attachment of the medial head of the gastrocnemius is also appreciated, kindly correlate clinically.

Grossly unremarkable remaining imaged extra-articular soft tissues.

MRI LEFT KNEE  (plain)

Clinical information:
Left knee pain and stiffness. Ultrasound shows a large complex collection at the posterior joint, MRI suggested. 

Technique: 
Multiplanar MR of the knee according to protocol.

Comparison: 
Ultrasound report dated [Date]

Findings: 

Menisci

Lateral meniscus: intact

Medial meniscus: Several tears of the medial meniscus noted. Radial tear close to the posterior root of the medial meniscus and another inferior surfacing horizontal tear is seen at the posterior horn. Radial tear with truncation also seen at the body of meniscus, which is attenuated in size. Most of the medial meniscus is extruded from the jointline, approximately 0.4cm medial to joint line. 

Ligaments

Anterior cruciate ligament: intact

Posterior cruciate ligament: intact 

Medial collateral ligament: Superficial and deep components intact. Thickening of the superificial component of the medial collateral ligament with moderate periligamentous edema is suggestive of moderate sprain. 

Lateral collateral ligament: The iliotibial band, biceps femoris tendon, fibular collateral ligament and popliteus muscle and tendon intact. 

Posterolateral corner structures: Intact

Extensor Mechanism

The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. The patella is normally positioned within the femoral groove. There is no retinacular disruption.

Fluid

Moderate knee effusion noted with evidence of synovitis. Thinned wall Baker's cyst with thin septations measuring 4.1cm x 3.4cm x 6.1cm (TSxAPxCC) is seen, consistent with a complex Bakers cyst. No fluid fluid level is seen..Small amount of fluid at the posterior knee is probably secondary to previous rupture.

Mild prepatellar bursitis observed. 

Osseous and Articular Structures

Bones: Mild oedema is seen at the anterior aspect of the medial tibial plateau. Moderate degenerative changes with osteophytosis of all three compartments noted. No fracture, stress reaction, or osseous lesion is seen.

Patellofemoral compartment: Full thickness chondral loss and fissures most observable at the patella apex and medial patella facet, associated with subchondral oedema. 

Medial compartment: Minimal chondrosis. 

Lateral compartment: Minimal chondrosis. 

Others:

Hoffas fat pad: clear

Muscles: Severe atrophy and fatty infiltration of the semimembranosus muscle. 

Neurovascular bundle: Normal 


COMMENT

1.	Multiloculated Bakers cyst with prior rupture. No evidence of haemorrhage or active inflammatory changes. 
2.	Several tears of the medial meniscus, including a radial tear of the posterior root, horizontal tear of the posterior horn and truncation of the inner free edge of the body of medial meniscus. Medial meniscal extrusion noted. 
3.	Moderate sprain of the superficial component of the medial collateral ligament. It is intact with no tear. 
4.	Severe patellofemoral chondral loss and fissures with subchondral oedema. Otherwise only minimal chondrosis at the tibiofemoral joint. Osteophytes in all three compartments.
5.	Mild prepatellar bursitis.
